title: Edge & Replicas
description: CDNs, replication and the consistency trade-offs that come with copies.

challenges.prompt: What does a CDN mainly serve?
options: Static content like images, video and JS from servers close to users
challenges.explanation: CDN edge servers around the world cache static files, so users get them from nearby and your origin servers never see those requests.

challenges.prompt: You add read replicas. What new problem can appear?
options: Replication lag: a read right after a write may return old data
challenges.explanation: Replicas copy changes asynchronously, so they can trail the primary. A common fix is read-your-own-writes: send a user's reads to the primary briefly after they write.

challenges.prompt: A video clip went viral. Most requests are for the same static thumbnails and video chunks. Keep the site up on a tight budget.
challenges.explanation: 60% of the traffic is static. A CDN absorbs it at the edge, leaving ~4,800 req/s for your servers. A cache then protects the database from the remaining reads.

challenges.prompt: A network partition splits your database cluster. According to CAP, what must you choose between?
challenges.explanation: During a partition, a node either refuses requests it cannot confirm (consistent) or answers with possibly stale data (available). Without a partition you can have both.

challenges.prompt: Which feature can most safely be eventually consistent?
challenges.explanation: Nobody is harmed if a like count lags by a second. Money, bookings and security settings need strong consistency.

challenges.prompt: In leader-follower replication, where do writes go?
options: To the leader, which then replicates them to followers
challenges.explanation: A single leader orders all writes, which avoids conflicts. Followers serve reads. If the leader dies, a follower is promoted.

challenges.prompt: Data is stored on N = 3 replicas. A write waits for W = 2 acknowledgements and a read asks R = 2 replicas. Why does this guarantee the read sees the latest write?
options: Because 2 is a majority of anything
Because W + R > N, so the read and write sets always overlap on at least one replica
Because reads are faster than writes
challenges.explanation: With W + R > N, any read set shares at least one replica with the last write set, so it is guaranteed to see the newest value.
